text: Bowland sheep, all facing the wrong way and each convinced it is the one who is right. {lead} circles once, low, and the whole flock goes through the gate like water. The farmer leaves a flask on the post.
A gap in a Swaledale wall, one stone short of a good afternoon. {lead} nudges the capstone back in, snug as a key in a lock, and the farmer, watching from the barn door, tips his cap.
A wheel of Lincolnshire Poacher, stuck in a rut. {lead} gives it a shove and down the slope it goes, round and round, and out of the hollow comes an old bus pass and a lot of loose change.
